label: rejected

evidence.V1: Silhouette reads as a broadleaf tree (lumpy round canopy on a single trunk) from front, three-quarter and top; generic lollipop but recognisable at 64 px.
evidence.V2: Big canopy + trunk read clearly, but medium/small detail is nearly absent: the two branch stubs are buried (only a tiny nub shows at the canopy underside) and there are no secondary leaf clumps.
evidence.V3: Trunk is a straight, untapered cylinder with a crude flared foot; canopy is one rounded blob - partly stylised, still stiff in the trunk.
evidence.V4: Root flare ends in sharp, razor-like jagged spikes (trunk_base close-up) while canopy is soft; edge treatment inconsistent across the asset.
evidence.V5: Canopy shows a visible quad-grid faceting pattern under studio light and the light-green top cap has a hard-edged boundary that reads as a pasted patch rather than a gradient; minor, no z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: foliage green in 2 values (mid + light top) and one bark brown; all colourways keep the same structure.
evidence.V7: 1604 tris vs tree target 2000 / ceiling 5000 - under target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material and kit-style palette, but faceted canopy and spiky root flare do not match the smooth fused-shell organic look of the kit - minor mismatch.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, Hull collision (trunk-only part option), CanTouch off, CastShadow on, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

artifacts: quad-grid faceting visible across canopy in studio light
hard-edged light-green cap on canopy top reads as a patch
jagged razor spikes on root flare at trunk base
top_fixes: Smooth the canopy (more subdivision or weighted normals) and blend the top highlight with a soft vertex-colour gradient instead of a hard cap
Add medium-scale detail: 2-3 secondary leaf clumps and visible branch forks so the canopy reads as more than one blob
Taper and slightly bend the trunk and rebuild the root flare as soft rounded buttress roots instead of sharp spikes
